extracted.intended_audience: writers (screenwriters, novelists, short-story writers, journalists, memoirists, narrative nonfiction writers)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for constructing effective narrative stories (especially for screenwriters) that center character transformation, moral vision, and original plotting; presents practical tools and techniques to shape plot, character, and theme. Useful across fiction and narrative non-fiction formats.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hero's moral and emotional growth
rubrics_metrics.description: Truby's method for constructing a story is at once insightful and practical, focusing on the hero's moral and emotional growth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make the protagonist's moral and emotional transformation central to the narrative arc; structure events and conflicts to provoke and reveal internal change rather than only external action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make the audience care about characters
rubrics_metrics.description: Writers will come away with specific, useful techniques to make the audience care about their characters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use concrete, actionable techniques (as opposed to vague advice) to create empathy and investment: reveal desires, stakes, contradictions, and vulnerabilities that invite audience identification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Characters must grow in meaningful ways
rubrics_metrics.description: Techniques that make their characters grow in meaningful ways.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure character arcs show real moral/emotional development tied to the story's conflicts and choices; avoid static or purely cosmetic change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Construct a surprising, concept-unique plot
rubrics_metrics.description: They will construct a surprising plot that is unique to their particular concept.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design plot developments that organically follow from the concept and character rather than relying on generic tropes; aim for surprises that arise from internal logic and moral stakes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Express a genuine moral vision
rubrics_metrics.description: They will learn how to express a moral vision that can genuinely move an audience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarify the story's thematic/moral position and weave it into character decisions and plot consequences so the audience experiences the moral argument rather than being told it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use an extremely precise set of tools
rubrics_metrics.description: Writers will come away with an extremely precise set of tools to work with--specific, useful techniques to make the audience care and to make characters grow.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer concrete techniques and structural devices (beats, scene functions, moral oppositions) over abstract 'rules'; apply these tools deliberately to solve story problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dig into personal values and worldviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Writers will dig deep within and explore their own values and worldviews in order to create an effective story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use self-examination to develop authentic moral conflicts and perspectives that inform character motivations and thematic depth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Build an effective, multifaceted narrative
rubrics_metrics.description: Truby offers a unique approach for how to build an effective, multifaceted narrative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Integrate plot, character, theme, and structure so each element reinforces the others; aim for layered meaning rather than single-thread storytelling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ground techniques in philosophy and mythology (use archetypal foundations)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Anatomy of Story draws on a broad range of philosophy and mythology, offering fresh techniques and insightful anecdotes alongside Truby's approach.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leverage archetypal motifs and philosophical/thematic patterns to enrich story resonance, while adapting them to the story's unique concept and characters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principles transferable across forms and genres
rubrics_metrics.description: The foundations of story that Truby lays out are so fundamental they are applicable--and essential--to all writers, from novelists and short-story writers to journalists, memoirists, and writers of narrative non-fiction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply the same core principles (character transformation, moral vision, precise tools, concept-driven plotting) across different media and genres, adapting tactics to format-specific constraints.
